simple.meaning: יָעֵף (yâʻêph) is a Hebrew object word meaning “fatigued ; figuratively, exhausted.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Samuel 16:2. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָעֵף (H3287) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: יָעֵף (yâʻêph) / H3287 is traced through 2 Samuel 16:2, Isaiah 40:29, Isaiah 50:4 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H3287. yaeph יָעֵף adjective weary, faint ; — always as substantive, except Judg 8:15 הַיְּפֵעִים אנשׁיך (of physical fatigue from lack of bread); הַיָּעֵף 2Sam 16:2 (from lack of drink); of mind and spirit Isa 40:29 (|| אוֺנִין אֵין ), 50:4 .
